reason: The cited evidence (all from the same paper) directly supports the formation, composition, diffusion mechanism, and hardness/wear improvements of the boride layer on a specific HEA. However, the key premise that this layer acts as a diffusion barrier against molten aluminum corrosion is not directly evidenced; the paper only speculates about corrosion resistance and cast aluminum applications without providing corrosion data.
premises: Powder-pack boriding of CoCrFeNiMn HEA forms a dense layer of MB and M2B borides
The boride layer forms by inward B diffusion and outward metal diffusion
The boride layer significantly increases surface microhardness (to ~23.8 GPa)
The boride layer improves wear resistance (lower friction coefficient)
Borides formed have excellent corrosion resistance, enabling use in cast aluminum industry applications
